notes: Counts refer to the 65 draft sentences; added replacement sentences (c66-c75) are all supported. Existing page entry: (1) 'diagnosis' gives HbA1c 48 mmol/mol / fasting glucose 7 mmol/L cut-offs; only NHS Scotland Right Decisions retrieved these (HbA1c 48 or more, fasting 7.0 or more, repeat if no symptoms), so they are supported by that page but not by NHS England text. (2) 'treatment' says metformin first, then SGLT2 inhibitors; the current NHS treatment page describes metformin together with an SGLT2 inhibitor as the usual starting point for people without other serious conditions (metformin alone first-line comes from older NICE/local formularies), so 'metformin first, then SGLT2 inhibitors' is at odds with the NHS page. (3) 'prevention' says programmes halve the risk in prediabetes: not retrieved/unsupported. (4) 'overview' says over 90% of diabetes is type 2 and that early weight loss can put it into remission: MedlinePlus gives 90-95% for the US; remission-through-weight-loss supported by Diabetes UK, but 'early' and 'over 90%' for the UK were not retrieved. (5) 'seekCare' says call 999 for chest pain, and same-day GP/NHS 111 for sudden vision change: not retrieved here; the NHS 999/A&E list retrieved was peeing a lot, very thirsty, feeling sick, confused/very sleepy, short of breath, and NHS inform wants urgent podiatrist/GP contact (NHS 111 if closed) for a hot, red, swollen foot or new skin damage. (6) 'riskFactors' age over 40 and South Asian/Black/Hispanic thresholds, and 'signs' acanthosis nigricans: not retrieved. Draft-specific: c36/c58 (non-urgent route for worsening vision) were marked unsafe because they conflict with the existing page's same-day advice for sudden vision change. The search budget (16) was fully used; pages not directly retrieved: NHS England Path to Remission evidence about remission rates, NHS England DVLA text. HbA1c cut-off numbers deliberately kept out of prose. Attribution caveats: the annual-review eye/urine details and the 'retinal photograph, not optician test' wording came from blended summaries (Diabetes UK annual review page listed first); MedlinePlus type 2 'gradually' and 'more common' claims were dropped from final text.
